examples.ko: 동생은 격투기 경기를 보는 것을 좋아해요.
examples.en: My younger brother likes watching combat sports matches.

examples.ko: 저는 운동 삼아 격투기를 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm learning a combat sport for exercise.
Combat sports athletes train every dawn.

examples.ko: 그 영화 주인공은 유명한 격투기 챔피언이에요.
examples.en: The hero of that movie is a famous combat sports champion.
These days combat sports gyms have opened in every neighborhood.

examples.ko: 격투기는 다치기 쉬워서 보호 장비가 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: Combat sports cause injuries easily, so protective gear is a must.

explain: 태권도나 유도처럼 하나의 무술 이름이 아니라, 권투·이종격투기처럼 서로 때리고 겨루는 종목을 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 종목 하나를 말할 때는 '권투', '레슬링'처럼 따로 불러요.
explain_en: Unlike 태권도 or 유도, this is not one martial art but a group name for sports where two people fight, such as boxing or mixed martial arts. For one specific sport people name it directly, like 권투 or 레슬링.

en: in the manner of rolling about

examples.en: On weekends, I want to lounge around on the sofa.
The cat rolls around lazily in the sunshine.

examples.ko: 방학 내내 뒹굴뒹굴 지냈더니 살이 쪘어요.
examples.en: I lazed around the whole vacation and gained weight.
I lounged around in bed and ended up oversleeping.
The kids roll around on the lawn, laughing.

examples.ko: 뒹굴뒹굴 만화책이나 보면서 보내고 싶은 날이에요.
examples.en: It's a day I want to spend lazing around reading comics.

explain: 하는 일 없이 편하게 누워 지내거나 이리저리 구르는 모습이에요. 푹 쉬는 느낌으로 좋게 쓰기도 하고 게으르다는 느낌으로 쓰기도 해요. '빈둥빈둥'은 일을 안 하고 노는 느낌이 더 부정적이에요.
explain_en: It describes lying around comfortably doing nothing, or rolling about. It can feel like pleasant resting or like laziness depending on context. '빈둥빈둥' is more negative, suggesting idling instead of working.

examples.en: Our team scored first in the first half.

examples.ko: 경기 시작 5분 만에 득점해서 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: We scored just five minutes into the game, and everyone was happy.

examples.ko: 축구에서는 공을 골대에 넣어야 득점할 수 있어요.
examples.en: In soccer, you can only score by getting the ball into the goal.

examples.ko: 두 번이나 득점한 선수가 오늘의 영웅이에요.
examples.en: The player who scored twice is today's hero.

examples.ko: 득점하는 순간 관중이 일어나서 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: The moment we scored, the crowd stood up and shouted.

examples.ko: 한 번 득점하고 나서 우리는 수비에 집중했어요.
examples.en: After scoring once, we focused on defense.

explain: 축구, 농구처럼 점수가 나는 경기에서 써요. 같은 상황에서 '골을 넣다', '점수를 내다'도 많이 말하고, '득점하다'는 뉴스와 중계에서 자주 들려요. 반대로 점수를 내줄 때는 '실점하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used in games where points are made, like soccer or basketball. In everyday speech people also say 골을 넣다 or 점수를 내다, while 득점하다 is common in news and commentary. The opposite, giving up points, is 실점하다.

examples.en: I exercise with dumbbells every morning.

examples.ko: 집에서 쓸 아령 두 개를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two dumbbells for home use.
If I hold dumbbells for long, my arms hurt.
I start with three-kilogram dumbbells.
Dumbbell exercises are good to do at home.
I put down the dumbbells and rested for a moment.

explain: 헬스장에서는 영어 외래어로 '덤벨'이라고도 많이 말해요. '아령 운동'이나 '아령을 들다'처럼 써요. 팔 힘을 기르는 작은 운동 기구예요.
explain_en: At the gym, people also often say the loanword '덤벨'. You say '아령 운동' or '아령을 들다'. It is a small piece of equipment for building arm strength.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 우스갯소리를 해서 사람들을 자주 웃겨요.
examples.en: My uncle often makes people laugh by telling jokes.
I said it as a joke, so please don't be angry.
The joke my grandfather told me was really funny.
I told a joke to lighten the mood.
That's just a joke, nothing more.

examples.ko: 요즘 인터넷에 도는 우스갯소리 들어 봤어요?
examples.en: Have you heard the joke going around the internet these days?

explain: '농담'은 '농담이야'처럼 진담이 아니라는 뜻으로도 쓰지만, '우스갯소리'는 웃기려고 하는 말이나 이야기에 더 가까워요. 줄여서 '우스개'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '농담' can mean 'I'm not serious' as in '농담이야', but '우스갯소리' is closer to a funny remark or story told to make people laugh. It can be shortened to '우스개'.

examples.en: I dove in the sea and saw fish.
The child likes to go underwater.
A haenyeo holds her breath and dives deep.
The submarine slowly began to dive.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 요즘 연락이 안 돼서 잠수했나 봐요.
examples.en: I can't reach him these days, so he must have disappeared.
Get your safety gear ready and then dive.

explain: '잠수하다'는 물속으로 깊이 들어갈 때 써요. 수영하다 물에 얼굴만 담그는 것은 보통 '잠수'라고 하지 않아요. 요즘은 말없이 연락이 끊겼을 때 '잠수 탔다', '잠수했다'라고 하는 쓰임도 많아요.

phrases.en: to go silent and cut off contact
phrases.nuance_ko: 물속에 숨은 것처럼 연락이 끊기고 사라진다는 말이에요. 친구나 연인 사이에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like someone hiding underwater, a person stops answering and disappears. It is casual, used among friends or couples.

explain_en: 잠수하다 is used for going deep under water. Just dipping your face in while swimming is not usually called 잠수. These days it is also widely used for someone who goes silent and cuts contact, as in 잠수 탔다.

examples.en: At Christmas, carols play on every street.
The children sing carols and wait for presents.
When December came, carols could be heard in every shop.

examples.ko: 캐럴은 12월에만 들을 수 있는 노래 같아요.
examples.en: Carols feel like songs you can only hear in December.
We are preparing a carol performance at church.

examples.ko: 캐럴에 맞춰 눈사람 인형이 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: The snowman doll danced to the carol.

explain: 캐럴은 크리스마스에 부르거나 트는 노래에만 써요. 다른 때는 '노래'나 '동요'를 써요. '캐롤'이 아니라 '캐럴'로 써야 맞아요.
explain_en: 캐럴 is only for songs sung or played at Christmas. At other times people say 노래 or 동요. The correct spelling is 캐럴, not 캐롤.

examples.en: The ping-pong ball rolled under the table.
A ping-pong ball is light and small, so it bounces well.
If you hit the ping-pong ball hard, it flies far.

examples.ko: 새 탁구공 세 개만 사다 주세요.
examples.en: Please buy me just three new ping-pong balls.
I wrote my name on my ping-pong ball.
A bump the size of a ping-pong ball appeared on my forehead.

explain: '탁구공만 한'처럼 크기를 비교하는 말에 자주 나와요. 같은 방식으로 '주먹만 한', '콩알만 한'도 써요. 공은 '한 개, 두 개'로 세요.
explain_en: It often appears in size comparisons like '탁구공만 한' (as big as a ping-pong ball). The same pattern works with '주먹만 한' (fist-sized) and '콩알만 한' (bean-sized). You count balls as '한 개, 두 개'.

examples.en: I learn tango every weekend.
Tango music is slow but intense.
The two people started dancing the tango.
Argentina is famous for tango.
I went to the theater to see a tango show.
In tango, two people must move as one.

explain: 춤 이름에는 '추다'를 써서 '탱고를 추다', '왈츠를 추다', '살사를 추다'처럼 말해요. '탱고를 치다'는 틀려요. 탱고는 음악 이름이기도 해서 '탱고 음악'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: Dances take the verb 추다: 탱고를 추다, 왈츠를 추다, 살사를 추다. 탱고를 치다 is wrong. 탱고 is also a music genre, so 탱고 음악 works too.

examples.ko: 우승 트로피를 두 손으로 들어 올렸어요.
examples.en: He lifted the winner's trophy with both hands.
There is a trophy on the bookshelf.
The player's name is engraved on the trophy.
I polish the trophy until it shines and keep it.
I received a trophy and a certificate together.
Even a small trophy is precious to me.

explain: 상을 받을 때 종이는 '상장', 돈은 '상금', 컵이나 조각 모양 물건은 '트로피'라고 따로 불러요. 보통 '트로피를 들어 올리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: When you win a prize, the paper is a 'sangjang', the money is 'sanggeum', and the cup or statue is a 'trophy'. People usually say 'teuropireul deureo ollida' (lift the trophy).

examples.en: My friend is a famous pianist.
The pianist came up on stage.
I have dreamed of being a pianist since I was young.
The pianist's hands were really fast.
That pianist performs in Korea every year.
Many young pianists gathered too.

explain: 직업으로 연주하는 사람에게 주로 써요. 취미로 치는 친구는 '피아노를 쳐요'라고 말해요. 바이올린 연주자는 '바이올리니스트'예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for someone who plays professionally. A friend who plays for fun is described as 피아노를 쳐요. A violin player is a 바이올리니스트.

examples.en: My younger sibling plays on the school hockey team.
I joined a club because I wanted to learn hockey.
I went to the field to watch a hockey game.
The hockey players practice hard every day.
I like soccer more than hockey.
I bought a new hockey stick.

explain: '하키'라고만 하면 보통 필드하키를 말하고, 얼음 위에서 하는 건 '아이스하키'라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: Plain '하키' usually means field hockey; the version played on ice is called '아이스하키'.
